findings.title: DreamHost Status: Investigating an incident affecting File Manager and Webmail
findings.summary_md: DreamHost's status page shows operations staff first reported connectivity issues affecting the File Manager interface at 2:20 p.m. PDT on October 23, 2026, with File Manager offline and some webmail users signed out by 5:20 p.m. PDT. As a precaution the company reset passwords for some email accounts and, by 10:13 p.m. PDT, extended the reset to FTP and SFTP users. The password reset for affected users was reported complete on October 24 at 10:37 a.m. PDT, with instruction emails sent in batches through the weekend.

findings.title: Active incident at Dreamhost forcing password reset
findings.summary_md: A Hacker News thread linking to the DreamHost status page reached 164 points, with commenters speculating that the File Manager, described as a Monsta FTP installation, may have been compromised through a recently published PHP vulnerability and that FTP credentials could have been exfiltrated. DreamHost's support chatbot reportedly denied a link to the PHP vulnerabilities, though commenters remained skeptical. The company had not published a root cause as of the thread.

findings.title: DreamHost resets some email and FTP passwords after outage
findings.summary_md: WhatsNewPaper reported that DreamHost reset passwords for some email and FTP/SFTP users after an incident that began October 23, 2026, affecting File Manager and webmail. The status page listed File Manager, email hosting, and webmail as disrupted while web hosting, the panel, billing, and other services remained operational. DreamHost advised customers to review each mailbox for unrecognized forwarding destinations and remove any they did not recognize.
